He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Old Dominion Monarchs basketball|Old Dominion Monarchs]], and appeared in one [[NBA]] game for the [[Indiana Pacers]]. ==High school career== Caver is the son of Wilton Caver. He attended [[Charles Drew High School]] in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]] as a freshman before transferring to [[North Gwinnett High School]] in [[Suwanee, Georgia]]. The move was made to become closer to his AAU coach [[Jerry Stackhouse]], who became his legal guardian. Caver spent his first season at North Gwinnett on the junior varsity team and grew to 5'10". After graduating from North Gwinnett, he did a [[postgraduate year]] at [[St. John's Northwestern Military Academy]], an experience he initially hated but his parents encouraged. He was lightly recruited, picking up an offer from [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Kent State]] before committing to [[Old Dominion Monarchs basketball|Old Dominion]].{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Ed |title=ODU guard Ahmad Caver went to great lengths to be noticed |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/sports/college/old-dominion/article_0629b91a-4c0f-5bf7-b297-dead28a0d598.html |accessdate=January 7, 2020 |work=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |date=February 17, 2017}} ==College career== Caver was a backup to [[Trey Freeman]] as a freshman, averaging 2.7 points per game and was named to the academic honor roll. Caver scored a season-high 26 points versus [[Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball|Marshall]] on January 5, 2017. As a sophomore, Caver led Old Dominion in scoring and assists with 13 points and 4.8 assists per game, to go with 3.5 rebounds per contest. He was named to the Third Team All-[[Conference USA]] and team MVP.{{cite news |title=ODU guard Ahmad Caver named to Preseason All-Conference USA team |url=https://wtkr.com/2017/10/19/odu-guard-ahmad-caver-named-to-preseason-all-conference-usa-team/ |accessdate=January 7, 2020 |work=WTKR |date=October 19, 2017}} He had a career-high 30 points on December 17, 2017, in an 82–77 overtime win over [[Fairfield Stags men's basketball|Fairfield]].{{cite news |title=Caver scores 30 in ODU's 82-77 OT win over Fairfield |url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/caver-scores-30-in-odu-s-82-77-ot-win-over-fairfield-121717 |accessdate=January 7, 2020 |work=[[Fox Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 17, 2017}} Caver averaged 14.2 points and 6.2 assists per game as a junior, leading the Monarchs to a 25–7 record and second place in conference. He was named to the First Team All-Conference USA and the league Defensive Team. Coming into his senior season, he was named to the [[Bob Cousy Award]] watchlist.{{cite news |title=ODU men's basketball picked third in C-USA preseason voting |url=https://augustafreepress.com/odu-mens-basketball-picked-third-in-c-usa-preseason-voting/ |accessdate=January 7, 2020 |work=[[Augusta Free Press]] |date=October 18, 2018}} As a senior, Caver averaged 16.6 points, 5.5 assists and 4.3 rebounds per game. Alongside [[B. J. Stith]], he helped lead Old Dominion to a Conference USA regular season championship and NCAA Tournament appearance.{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Ed |title="I have a dream I want to accomplish." Former ODU guard Ahmad Caver signs with Memphis Grizzlies |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/sports/college/old-dominion/vp-sp-odu-basketball-caver-memphis-20191015-ht2jngiu4bbu7goxijtdg4yoey-story.html |accessdate=January 7, 2020 |work=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |date=October 15, 2019}} Caver was named to the First Team All-Conference USA. He finished his college career ranked eighth in conference history in assists (607) and 15th in steals (187).{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Ahmad Caver|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-ahmad-caver-191015|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2019|accessdate=October 15, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Memphis Hustle (2019–2021)=== Caver signed with sports agent DeAngelo Simmons in preparation for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but went undrafted. He signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on October 15, 2019. On October 16, he was cut by the Grizzlies and joined the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite news|title=Ahmad Caver: Cut by Memphis|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/ahmad-caver-cut-by-memphis/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=October 16, 2019|access-date=January 7, 2020}} Caver contributed 23 points and four assists in a 120–112 loss to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] on March 7, 2020.{{cite news|title=Jack Scores 31 To Lead Skyforce Past Hustle|url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20200307/mhusxf/|work=NBA.com|date=March 7, 2020|access-date=May 3, 2020}} He averaged 9.9 points, 4 assists and 3.3 rebounds per game for the Hustle.{{cite news|title=Ahmad Caver: Drops 23 points in loss|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/ahmad-caver-drops-23-points-in-loss/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=June 15, 2020}} On December 11, 2020, Caver signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Ahmad Caver|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-ahmad-caver-201211|website=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2020|access-date=December 13, 2020}} He was waived at the end of training camp and returned to the Hustle. During the 2020–21 season, Caver averaged 16.5 points, 4.1 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.9 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Schmidt |first1=Dakota |title=Ahmad Caver Named Ridiculous Upside's 2021 G League Most Improved Player of the Year |url=https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2021/4/23/22398668/ahmad-caver-named-ridiculous-upsides-2021-g-league-most-improved-player-of-the-year-memphis-hustle |website=Ridiculous Upside |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=October 25, 2021 |date=April 23, 2021}} On October 14, 2021, Caver again signed with the Grizzlies,{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Ahmad Caver and Matthew Hurt|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-ahmad-caver-and-matthew-hurt-211014#|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=October 15, 2021}} but was waived three days later, prior to the start of the season.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign David Stockton|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-david-stockton-211015#|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 16, 2021}} On October 23, he re-signed with the Hustle.{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Moore|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2021-22 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster-211023/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} Caver averaged 15.4 points, 7.0 assists and 4.5 rebounds per game. ===Indiana Pacers (2021–2022)=== On December 31, 2021, Caver signed a 10-day contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]] via the hardship exemption.{{cite news |title=Region/state roundup: Pacers to sign former ODU guard Ahmad Caver to 10-day hardship deal, according to report |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/sports/vp-sp-region-state-0101-20211231-t6ggac2vszh3fbq6so2s47ftja-story.html |access-date=December 31, 2021 |work=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |date=December 31, 2021}} He made his NBA debut on January 5, 2022, scoring two points in a 129–121 loss against the [[2021–22 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite news |author1=James Boyd |title=Pacers Ahmad Caver's first NBA points cost some bettors a lot of money |url=https://eu.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2022/01/10/pacers-ahmad-caver-scores-first-nba-points-upsets-bettors/9152806002/ |access-date=26 March 2022 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |date=10 January 2022}} ===Return to the Memphis Hustle (2022)=== On January 10, 2022, Caver was reacquired and activated by the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 10, 2022|access-date=January 10, 2022}} In 43 games played (41 starts), he averaged 16.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 7.5 assists and 1.7 steals per game. Caver joined the [[Phoenix Suns]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Phoenix Suns 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612756/suns |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===BC Wolves (2022–2023)=== On August 6, Caver signed with [[BC Wolves]] of the [[Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL).{{cite news |title=BC Wolves inks Ahmad Caver |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bc-wolves-inks-ahmad-caver/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 6, 2022 |date=August 6, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} On May 10, 2023, Caver received the [[LKL Most Valuable Player Award|LKL Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) award after averaging 16.9 points, 3.3 rebounds, 5.8 assists and 1.9 steals in 31 regular season games played, leading the league in points and efficiency.{{cite web|title=Playoff matchups confirmed as Betsafe-LKL regular season wraps up|url=https://en.lkl.lt/straipsniai/6729/playoff-matchups-confirmed-as-betsafe-lkl-regular-season-wraps-up|website=lkl.lt|date=May 10, 2023|accessdate=May 11, 2023}} On July 20, 2023, Caver signed with [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/819820/H.Holon-adds-Caver-to-their-roster|title=H.Holon adds Caver to their roster|last=|first=|date=July 20, 2023|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=August 6, 2023}} On October 28, 2023, he left the club over concerns about the security situation in Israel, without appearing in a game for Hapoel Holon.{{cite web|title=Ahmad Caver leaves Hapoel Holon|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/ahmad-caver-leaves-hapoel-holon/|website=Sportando|date=October 28, 2023|accessdate=October 30, 2023}} ===JDA Dijon (2023–2024)=== On November 1, 2023, Caver signed with [[JDA Dijon Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jda-bourgogne-dijon-officially-signs-ahmad-caver/|title=JDA Bourgogne Dijon officially signs Ahmad
